chunks: Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim al-Sarraj narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from Hassan al-Basri, from Mu'awiah ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: O Mu'awiah! Do not leave visiting the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) due to fear, for whoever leaves it will see such regret that he will wish his grave were next to him.
Do you not love that Allah sees your person and your blackness (or distinctiveness) among those for whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), 'Ali, Fatimah, and the Imams pray?
Do you not love to be among those who return with forgiveness for what has passed, and for whom the sins of seventy years are forgiven?
Do you not love to be among those who leave this world with no sin that will be pursued (against them)?
Do you not love to be tomorrow among those whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) will shake hands with?

key_terms.صَفِيحَة: Shaking hands (a sign of honor in the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and benefits of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s encouragement to Mu'awiah ibn Wahb to overcome fear when visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn, framing it as a means to secure intercession from the Ahl al-Bayt. This tradition highlights the theological concept of 'Ziyarat' as a spiritual conduit for divine mercy, promising the forgiveness of seventy years of sins and the unique honor of being greeted by the Prophet on the Day of Resurrection.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym Al-Sarrāj narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from Ghassān Al-Basri, from Mu’āwiyah ibn Wahab, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

O Mu’āwiyah! Do not neglect going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) because of fear. Verily he who abandons the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) (for any reason) will regret it so much that he will wish that his grave was next to him.
Do you not like Allāh to see you among those for whom the Messenger of Allāh, ‘Ali, Fāťimah, and the Imams (a.s.) pray?!
Do you not like to be among those who return with forgiveness for their past sins and (do you not like) to return from his Ziyārah with seventy years of sins forgiven for you?!
Do you not like to be among those who will not have any sins about which they will be questioned when they leave this life?!
Do you not like to be among those whose hands the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) will shake tomorrow (on the Day of Judgment)?!
